published_prior_art.cite: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention — iterative oracle CDIS is specified, but no finite SI-rule encoding or total closure-runtime certificate is given.
DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention leaves CDIS completeness open; Zhang2008CompleteFCI and JaberKocaogluShanmugamBareinboim2020 do not require one common basal selected DAG across all regimes.
DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention, Theorem 3 proves soundness only and expressly leaves completeness uncertain.
DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention provides a sound CDIS output, not a complete coupled-regime SI-PAG procedure with certified oracle-input closure cost.
DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention supplies the selected-versus-directed compatible pair; its canonical SI-PAG endpoint reading is a boundary corollary.
Zhang2008CompleteFCI supplies the ordinary complete-FCI baseline; the K=0, no-selection collapse is a required sanity corollary.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:compatible-input; Open-ended Question 1 and Theorems 1–2
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: All semantic and algorithmic conclusions are conditional on the supplied oracle regime-MAG family admitting at least one model in the Dai compatibility class.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The canonical SI-PAG equality, paired-witness conclusion, and closure certificate hold for compatible oracle families M with C_D(M) nonempty.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3–8, Definition 1, Theorem 2, Theorem 3, and the completeness paragraph following Theorem 3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines pre-intervention selection through interventional twin graphs, characterizes its special equivalence class by regime-MAG adjacencies and v-structures, proves CDIS soundness, and states that completeness remains uncertain.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1–3 and 7, intervention-mechanism setup, no-selection assumption, Lemma 1, and Theorem 3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper treats unknown-target mechanism changes, explicitly assumes no selection bias, establishes an augmented-I-MAG realization lemma, and proves Psi-FCI completeness.
The article states that augmented FCI orientation rules are complete under the standard latent-confounding and selection-bias setting for an ordinary ancestral-graph equivalence class.

The paper studies restrictions of one MAG Markov-equivalence class by expert edge-mark knowledge, provides sound orientation rules and setting-specific representation results, plus a checking algorithm outside those settings.

The paper gives polynomial-delay listing of MAGs in one MEC using singleton background knowledge and locally complete rules, while noting that general background-knowledge completeness remains unresolved.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a generic non-two-variable obstruction family in which individually valid regime-wise MAG completions cannot arise from a common basal selected DAG and ordered target family; make the obstruction a corollary of the paired-realizability lemma.
Give one fully worked small oracle-MAG instance that displays the initial family, each cross-regime rule firing, the closure certificate, and the two witnesses for one residual circle.

State a conservative syntactic upper bound on the maximum regime and vertex placeholder counts needed by the final finite rule list, so the polynomial closure certificate is immediately executable rather than merely parametric in the rules.

recommended_next_step: Advance this repaired, field-grade proposal to Stage 0; retain the compatible-oracle condition as the settled scope boundary.
